findings.observation: Frames 37–56 show readable native Standard table, Leave table and Show hand controls with Moon table round 2 / Your turn / Orbit claimed 3 Moons. The actual hand and lower game content are outside the captured viewport. Frame 57 wraps Standard table into two readable lines in the narrower split pane.
findings.limit: Visible text fit is not an interaction or accessibility qualification.

findings.observation: Frames 60–76 show Compose public round/claim content in the left split pane. The instruction beginning Only a challenge reveals the is cut at the bottom viewport edge; the hand and Show hand control are not visible. This does not positively verify a concealed Compose hand or scroll/control reachability.

No exposed game card faces were seen in the directly inspected payloads; every repeated source identity was independently proven byte-equal to a direct reference. The card hand itself is outside the captured ready/return viewports.
No leave-table confirmation dialog is visible in any reviewed source-frame payload. The table-style chooser at the start is a different visible dialog.
The native ready and Compose return views both show Moon table, round 2, Your turn and an Orbit three-Moons claim. This is visual consistency of public text only.

conclusion: All retained source identities have direct or verified exact-byte-match coverage. Opaque transition covers and no exposed card faces or leave confirmation are observed in these retained pixels. The ready/returned hand lies outside the captured viewport, so concealed-hand return and interaction/accessibility acceptance are not established. Bottom-edge text clipping is recorded as a viewport observation, not a proven reachability defect.
limits: This review covers retained decoded source-frame identities only; it does not establish continuous privacy between captured frames or outside these clips.
Original MP4 packet PTS and time base are preserved. No alignment to host UTC, on-screen clock, automation action time, or display/compositor event time is inferred.

The native ready screen shows a Show hand control, but the hand itself is outside the captured viewport. These pixels do not establish a reveal/reconceal test or what was rendered outside the viewport.
Clipping at the bottom viewport edge is a visible layout observation, not proof that content or controls are unreachable. No scrolling or tapping was executed during this review.
